01 / Product capability

Fixed, exclusive, and predictable by design

A static datacenter endpoint gives one business system a stable source IP. It is designed for target-system allowlists, environment isolation, long sessions, and consistent network routing rather than frequent IP rotation.

Fixed dedicated IP

Keep the same datacenter exit throughout the active service period.

Unmetered traffic

Do not accumulate transferred GB for long-running tasks.

Stable bandwidth

Use clear 5–10Mbps endpoint specifications.

Datacenter performance

Prioritize predictable connectivity and cost.

Credential authentication

Connect with the assigned proxy username and password.

24/7 operation

Support production systems and continuous automation.

06 / Developer access

Manage fixed endpoints as infrastructure assets

Store proxy credentials in system configuration, register the source IP where required, and monitor connectivity and renewal. No rotation logic is needed in application code.

Standard HTTP proxy configurationExplicit timeout and retry policyProduction monitoring by workload
Python
import requests

proxy = "http://customer-static:YOUR_PASSWORD@38.91.24.27:8080"
proxies = {"http": proxy, "https": proxy}

response = requests.get(
    "https://target.example/data",
    proxies=proxies,
    timeout=20,
)

print(response.status_code)
07 / FAQ

Questions to answer before production

Validate the product boundary, package model, target behavior, and capacity with representative requests.

Does the IP rotate automatically?

No. The IP remains fixed during the active purchase and renewal period.

Does unmetered traffic have a bandwidth limit?

Yes. Unmetered means no per-GB billing; each endpoint still has a bandwidth specification such as 5–10Mbps.

How is this different from static residential proxy?

Datacenter proxies prioritize performance, stability, and cost. Static residential proxies also provide residential ISP network identity.

Can I register the exit IP in a target-system allowlist?

Yes. The exit remains fixed and can be registered with the target system. Access to the proxy itself still uses the assigned username and password.

Is it designed for frequent IP changes?

No. Use a rotating proxy product when the workload requires a large changing IP pool.
